dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:1801.text: To patch the bottom of a shoe. Formed from 革, with 丁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1802.text: The ball used in kicking-ball play. Formed from 革, with 匊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1803.text: A small hand drum shaken by its handle, whose side pellets strike its faces. Formed from 革, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1804.text: A vessel for measuring things. Another explanation: a bucket for drawing water from a well; anciently made of leather. Formed from 革, with 冤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1805.text: A knife sheath. Formed from 革, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1806.text: The leather at the front of a carriage is called 鞎. Formed from 革, with 艮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1807.text: A carriage's front crossbar. Formed from 革, with 弘 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “A leather-covered crossbar and a shallow carriage cover.” Read like 穹.

shuowen:1808.text: A binding around a carriage axle. Formed from 革, with 敄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1809.text: A carriage binding. Formed from 革, with 必 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1810.text: The leather bindings fitted to a carriage pole or crossbar. The received text distinguishes bent and straight shafts. Formed from 革, with 爨 indicating the sound; pronounced like 鑽 in the Analects. [Duan argues the received numeral three should be five, and that the technical descriptions are damaged.]

shuowen:1811.text: The cords of a canopy pole. Formed from 革, with 旨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1812.text: Carriage harness equipment. Formed from 革, with 皮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1813.text: A bridle, particularly the straps encircling a horse’s head. Formed from 革, with 弇 indicating the sound. Read like 譍.

shuowen:1814.text: The leather of a bridle. Formed from 革, with 巴 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1815.text: Leather harness straps that pass beneath or near a horse’s flanks. Formed from 革, with 顯 indicating the sound. [Duan argues both the anatomical term and the cross-referenced strap-name in the received text are corrupted.]

shuowen:1816.text: A strap across the breast. Formed from 革, with 斤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1817.text: Harness equipment for a side horse in a team. Formed from 革, with 𧈪 indicating the sound. The text gives readings resembling 騁 and 蜃. [Duan finds the second pronunciation clause corrupt.]

shuowen:1818.text: A strap that pulls the axle. Formed from 革, with 引 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1819.text: Carriage harness equipment. Formed from 革, with 官 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1820.text: Carriage harness equipment. Formed from 革, with 豆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1821.text: A leather loop or strap fitted within a carriage axle cap. Formed from 革, with 于 indicating the sound. [Duan questions the transmitted first component-name 輨.]

shuowen:1822.text: A rope beneath a carriage. Formed from 革, with 尃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1823.text: Carriage equipment. Formed from 革, with 奄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1824.text: Carriage equipment. Formed from 革, with 叕 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1825.text: Horse harness equipment, a saddle. Formed from 革 and 安.

shuowen:1826.text: Furry saddle ornamentation. Formed from 革, with 茸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1827.text: Saddle ornamentation. Formed from 革, with 占 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1828.text: A protection against sweat. Formed from 革, with 合 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1829.text: The headgear and bit of a horse. Formed from 革, with 力 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1830.text: Leather binding the yoke of a large cart. Formed from 革, with 肙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1831.text: The leather of a bridle. Formed from 革, with 面 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1832.text: A leather shoe or strap, related to 鞮 or 鞻. Formed from 革, with 今 indicating the sound. [Duan suspects the entry may be a later insertion into Shuowen.]

shuowen:1833.text: That which stores bows and arrows. Formed from 革, with 建 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1834.text: A case for bows and arrows. Formed from 革, with 𧷏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1835.text: A hanging tassel. Formed from 革, with 巂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1836.text: Tight or urgent. Formed from 革, with 亟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1837.text: To drive on. Formed from 革, with 𠊳 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1838.text: A leather neck strap. Formed from 革, with 央 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1839.text: The cord of a worn knife. Formed from 革, with 蒦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1840.text: A horse's tail strap, now called 般緧. Formed from 革, with 它 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1841.text: To bind a cow's shank. Formed from 革, with 見 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1842.text: A knife sheath. Formed from 革, with 肖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1843.text: Horse harness equipment. Formed from 革, with 薦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1844.text: A kind of leather shoe. Formed from 革, with 華 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1845.text: A horse's bridle. Formed from 革, with 勺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1846.text: A kind of tripod holding five 觳. One dou and two sheng make a 觳. It depicts a patterned belly and three legs. All characters in the 鬲 category are formed from 鬲.

shuowen:1847.text: A three-legged cauldron. Another explanation: a vessel for soaking rice. Formed from 鬲, with 支 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1848.text: A three-legged cauldron with a handle and spout. Read like 嬀. Formed from 鬲, with 規 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1849.text: A kind of cauldron. Formed from 鬲, with 㚇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1850.text: In Qin, an earthenware cauldron is called 𩰫. Formed from 鬲, with 𡕒 indicating the sound. Read like 過.

shuowen:1851.text: A large cauldron. Another explanation: a tripod broad above and narrow below, like a steamer, is called 鬵. Formed from 鬲, with 兓 indicating the sound. Read like 岑.

shuowen:1852.text: A kind of 鬵 cauldron. Formed from 鬲, with 曾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1853.text: A kind of cauldron. Formed from 鬲, with 甫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1854.text: A kind of 鬲 cooking vessel. Formed from 鬲, with 虍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1855.text: Cooking vapor rising. Formed from 鬲, with abbreviated 蟲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1856.text: The appearance of cooking vapor. Formed from 鬲, with 嚻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1857.text: To boil. Formed from 鬲, with 羊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1858.text: To boil. Formed from 鬲, with 沸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1859.text: A vessel for cooking, also an archaic form of 鬲. It depicts cooking vapors rising from the vessel. All characters in the 䰜 category are formed from the same cooking-vessel graph. [Duan considers the transmitted initial 㽁 gloss an interpolation.]

shuowen:1860.text: Gruel. Formed from 𩰲, with 侃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1861.text: Thick gruel, 䭈. Formed from 𩰲, with 米 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1862.text: Thick gruel, 䭈. Formed from 𩰲, with 古 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1863.text: Soup with the five flavors harmonized. Formed from 𩰲 and 羔. The Odes says: “There is also harmonious soup.”

shuowen:1864.text: The vegetable ingredients placed in a cooking cauldron, such as bamboo shoots and cattail shoots; in Chenliu dialect it could refer to a rice-based stew or thick porridge. Formed from 𩰲, with 速 indicating the sound. [Duan regards the transmitted 葦 (“reeds”) as a variant of 筍 (“bamboo shoots”), and the source gloss is damaged.]

shuowen:1865.text: Gruel. Formed from 𩰲, with 毓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1866.text: In Liangzhou, gruel is called 𩱸. Formed from 𩰲, with 𥽘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1867.text: Cakes made from meal. Formed from 𩰲, with 耳 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1868.text: To simmer or roast, 𤎅. Formed from 𩰲, with 芻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1869.text: To put meat and vegetables in hot water and take them out after a short time. Formed from 𩰲, with 翟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1870.text: To boil or cook food in a vessel. Formed from 𩰲, with 者 indicating the sound. [Duan suggests that the transmitted gloss 孚 is corrupt and should refer to cooking (𩰱).]

shuowen:1871.text: A blowing sound as liquid boils. Formed from 𩰲, with 孛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1872.text: To grasp. A hand turned downward is called 爪. A pictograph. All characters in the 爪 category are formed from 爪.

shuowen:1873.text: To hatch eggs. Formed from 爪 and 子. Another explanation: trustworthiness.

shuowen:1874.text: A macaque. This creature likes to use its claws; 爪 represents the macaque, and the lower belly depicts its form. Wang Yu says: “爪 is pictographic.”

shuowen:1875.text: Also to grasp. Formed from reversed 爪. The explanation is incomplete.

shuowen:1876.text: To hold. It depicts a hand grasping and taking hold of something. All characters in the 丮 category are formed from 丮. Read like 𢧢.

shuowen:1877.text: To sow or cultivate plants, especially grain. Formed from 坴 and 丮, depicting hands taking seeds and planting them. The Documents says: “I sowed millet and panicled millet.”

shuowen:1878.text: Cooked food. Formed from 丮, with 𦎫 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “Cooked food.”

shuowen:1879.text: To set out cooked food. Formed from 丮 and 食, with 才 indicating the sound. Read like 載.

shuowen:1880.text: To embrace. Formed from 丮, with 工 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1881.text: To prop, grasp or pull against something, in the sense of 掎 (“to hold back or pull”). Formed from 丮, with 𧮫 indicating the sound. [Duan corrects the transmitted 踦 to 掎.]

shuowen:1882.text: To strike the ankle. Formed from 丮 and 戈. Read like 踝.

shuowen:1883.text: To drag while holding. Formed from reversed 丮. The explanation is incomplete.

shuowen:1884.text: Two warriors facing each other, weapons behind them: it depicts fighting. All characters in the 鬥 category are formed from 鬥.

shuowen:1885.text: To meet or encounter. Formed from 鬥, with 𣂪 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1886.text: To fight. Formed from 鬥, with 共 indicating the sound. The Mencius says: “Zou and Lu fought.”

shuowen:1887.text: To kill by strangling with twisted cord. Formed from 鬥, with 翏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1888.text: To contend and take. Formed from 鬥, with 龜 indicating the sound. Read like 糾, a three-stranded rope.

shuowen:1889.text: Little intelligence and inferior strength. Formed from 鬥, with 爾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1890.text: Fighting entangled together, confusedly pulling one another. Formed from 鬥, with 燹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1891.text: To fight. Formed from 鬥, with abbreviated 賓 indicating the sound. Read like 賓.

shuowen:1892.text: Continual contention. The Odes says: “Brothers quarrel within the walls.” Formed from 鬥 and 兒; 兒 is one adept at contention.

shuowen:1893.text: A hammer used to test a strongman's strength. Formed from 鬥 and 戈; alternatively from abbreviated 戰. Read like 縣.

shuowen:1894.text: Unquiet. Formed from 市 and 鬥.

shuowen:1895.text: A hand. A pictograph. It has three fingers because representations of the many divisions of a hand are abbreviated to no more than three. All characters in the 又 category are formed from 又.

shuowen:1896.text: Hand and mouth assisting one another. Formed from 又 and 口.

shuowen:1897.text: The upper arm. Formed from 又 and an ancient written form.

shuowen:1898.text: Fingers crossing one another. Formed from 又, depicting a forked form.

shuowen:1899.text: Nails of the hands and feet. Formed from 又, depicting the shape of nails.

shuowen:1900.text: A rule or standard: the head of a household who leads and teaches. Formed from 又 raising a staff.
